title: Treasury Repurchase Agreement Risk Management FAQs

source.name: Federal Reserve Bank of New York

summary: The Treasury Market Practices Group (TMPG) released FAQs on May 22, 2025, clarifying recommended best practices for Treasury repo risk management, including the application of haircuts or margin on repos alongside other risk management techniques. The guidance aims to address inconsistencies in bilateral repo market risk management and potential systemic risks from leverage that may not be properly priced or risk managed.
key_points: TMPG recommends that all Treasury repos should be subject to prudent risk management, including application of haircuts (or margin) on the value of securities
Current bilateral repo market risk management practices lack consistency and transparency, and full leverage in the repo market may not be understood or properly priced by market participants
Large quantities of repos without prudent risk management could pose systemic risks to overall market functioning if one or more market participants default
Implementation deadline: TMPG recommends firms implement the best practice by June 2026 using a risk-based rolling approach prioritizing most material counterparty exposures
Centrally cleared repos already adhere to the recommended best practice through existing CCP margining/risk management regimes
Legal agreements must be enforceable and describe margining regime, valuation of exposures and collateral, and close-out netting procedures
why_it_matters: The TMPG guidance addresses systemic risks in the Treasury repo market, where inconsistent risk management practices in bilateral repo create potential for cascading defaults during market stress. This guidance codifies minimum risk management standards (haircuts, margin, legal documentation) that will become standard practice ahead of mandatory central clearing implementation.
market_structure_context: The document directly addresses market plumbing issues: bilateral repo market risk management inconsistencies, leverage opacity, and systemic risk concerns. Recommends haircuts/margin as counterparty credit and liquidity risk mitigation. Central clearing expansion (SEC rule amendments) is acknowledged as ongoing but not fully addressing NCCBR market risks. Implementation of best practices scheduled for June 2026.
